newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up, foreign investors hold key.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up, foreign investors hold key.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed on Thursday, continuing recent advances, but traders said the short-term outlook for the market depended to a large part on the strategy of foreign investors.
"Everyone is watching foreign investors to see what will be their next step and to follow their lead," said Matej Golob, a trader at brokerage Bema.
The SBI index rose 6.34 points or 0.50 percent to 1,271.8. The index has rebounded 42.6 percent since September 10, when it hit an all-time low.
Golob said the market appeared to be entering a period of consolidation following the heady gains.
Turnover fell to 329.4 million tolars from 610.7 million. Overall 10 shares rose, nine fell and one was unchanged. Four shares did not trade.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, firming 2.17 percent to close at 42,400 tolars on volume of 3,140 shares for total turnover of 132.9 million tolars.
Bank UBK was the biggest gainer, jumping 9.59 percent to 8,000 tolars. Traders downplayed the move, however, noting that volume was extremely low at five lots.

Financial consultancy Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 9.53 percent to 24,200 tolars on volume of 227 shares for total turnover of 5.6 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
